incidents.vector: Attackers obtained a leaked token granting access to Grafana Labs' GitHub environment and downloaded the company's codebase before being detected.
incidents.impact: Grafana publicly refused to pay the ransom, citing FBI guidance. The company says no customer data, personal information or production systems were accessed and the compromised credentials have been invalidated. CoinbaseCartel — a data-theft offshoot of the Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters collective — has now extorted more than 100 companies since September.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia, and the UK
incidents.vector: Vishing callers impersonating IT help desks lure employees to lookalike SSO portals (e.g. .enrollms[.]com, .passkeyms[.]com) where credentials and MFA codes are relayed in real time to the legitimate provider, then attackers register their own MFA device for persistence and run Python/PowerShell to exfiltrate SharePoint and OneDrive data via Microsoft Graph.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group tracks the actor as UNC6671 / 'BlackFile,' a distinct cluster from ShinyHunters that has co-opted the brand for credibility. In one engagement the group used a single Python script to pull over a million files from a victim's SharePoint/OneDrive. Initial extortion demands are in the millions; refusal escalates to Gmail spam floods, threatening voicemails to executives, and swatting.

incidents.vector: An unauthenticated attacker sends crafted requests exploiting CVE-2026-20182, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager, to log in as a high-privileged non-root user, then adds SSH keys, modifies NETCONF and escalates to root. Separate clusters are also chaining three older bugs (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122) to drop XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder webshells, AdaptixC2 beacons, Sliver implants and XMRig miners.
incidents.impact: Talos clusters the CVE-2026-20182 activity as UAT-8616, a highly sophisticated actor whose infrastructure overlaps with Operational Relay Box (ORB) networks frequently used by state-sponsored operators. SD-WAN controllers sit in the middle of east-west enterprise traffic, making them high-value pre-positioning targets. ACSC and CISA have flagged the activity as critical.

incidents.victim: TanStack, Mistral, UiPath, OpenAI, and ~400 npm packages
incidents.vector: Compromised npm packages of the TanStack React framework injected a self-propagating worm ('Mini Shai-Hulud') that stole credentials, used them to publish trojanized versions of any package the developer had access to, and wiped systems when tokens were rotated.
incidents.impact: The worm spread to almost 400 npm libraries within hours, including packages at AI company Mistral and automation vendor UiPath. OpenAI confirmed two employees were affected and rotated code-signing certificates, with the malware accessing a small number of repositories but no user data. Two days later TeamPCP released the worm's source code on Breached[.]st with a $10,000 reward for the largest follow-on attack, virtually guaranteeing a wave of copycat campaigns.

incidents.vector: Lapsus$ stole internal source code from Vodafone; the company refused to pay and the data was published on the group's leak site.
incidents.impact: Source-code leak with reputational and supply-chain risk for downstream Vodafone services. Vodafone has not detailed the access vector publicly.

incidents.vector: An attacker maintained access to Best Western's reservation systems for over six months between October 2025 and April 2026; the initial vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Best Western is notifying guests of multiple brands — Best Western, Sure Hotels, WorldHotels — that personal and reservation data may have been exposed. The six-month dwell time and reservation-system access suggest a substantial PII exposure.

incidents.vector: The Nitrogen ransomware group breached Foxconn's North American manufacturing environment and ran a double-extortion attack (data theft followed by encryption).
incidents.impact: Production at Foxconn's North American factories — which assemble products for Apple, Google and NVIDIA — was disrupted; Nitrogen claims it stole 8 TB of data including confidential project drawings and chip designs. Foxconn has confirmed the incident publicly.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Skoda's German web store to access customer data; the company has not detailed the bug.
incidents.impact: Skoda confirmed customer data was likely accessed via the e-commerce platform. Scope of records exposed has not been published.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious Ruby packages were published over two days specifically designed to attack RubyGems engineers and staff, attempting cross-site scripting and data theft from their systems.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups in response and is investigating what attackers tried to steal from staff. The incident is unrelated to but contemporaneous with the TanStack/Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm.

incidents.vector: An unidentified ransomware operator breached West's network in early May, stealing data and encrypting systems used to ship, receive and manufacture injectable drug-delivery components.
incidents.impact: West, a $3B/year supplier of stoppers, seals and components for injectable medicines, disclosed the incident via SEC 8-K. Global manufacturing, shipping and receiving were disrupted; operations have been partially restored.

incidents.vector: Pro-Palestinian hacktivist group The 313 Team launched a sustained DDoS attack against Chime's online banking service.
incidents.impact: Chime fended off the attack but customers have filed a class-action lawsuit alleging the company failed to maintain availability of online banking services. The same group has previously taken down Canonical/Ubuntu, BlueSky and Mastodon.

incidents.vector: Schemata, an AI virtual training platform serving the Department of Defense, exposed an unauthenticated API online that leaked U.S. service member records and sensitive military training documents.
incidents.impact: Security firm Strix discovered the leak; Schemata took 150 days to secure the API. The exposed data includes personnel records and sensitive military training materials — a substantial defense-information exposure even though no attacker appears to have weaponized the access.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters re-exploited the same 'Free-For-Teacher' account issue twice within a week to access Instructure's Canvas platform, exfiltrate data and deface login pages at thousands of schools and universities with a public ransom demand.
incidents.impact: 3.65 TB of data on roughly 275 million students and faculty at nearly 9,000 institutions was stolen. The defacement during final exams forced Canvas offline. Instructure ultimately paid the ransom and received 'digital confirmation of data destruction.' The Instructure CEO has been summoned to testify before the House Homeland Security Committee.

incidents.vector: A state-suspected cluster Unit 42 tracks as CL-STA-1132 exploited CVE-2026-0300, an unauthenticated buffer-overflow zero-day in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal (Captive Portal), to gain root RCE on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls. Post-exploit, attackers injected shellcode into the nginx worker, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, ran Active Directory enumeration with credentials taken from the firewall, and systematically deleted logs.
incidents.impact: First exploitation attempts began April 9; successful RCE on April 16; a SAML flood was used to fail-over to a second device and compromise it too. Prisma Access, Cloud NGFW and Panorama are unaffected. Risk is highest where the Captive Portal is exposed to the internet — a typical pre-positioning target on edge devices that lack endpoint logging.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the DAEMON Tools download site and signed trojanized installers with the vendor's legitimate code-signing certificate from at least April 8. The first-stage implant fingerprints each victim (MAC, hostname, locale, DNS domain, processes, installed software) and uploads to an attacker server; a second-stage QUIC RAT is deployed only on selected high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed several thousand stage-1 infections but the second-stage RAT landed on only about a dozen government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus and Thailand — the same surgical, targeted-supply-chain pattern previously used against Notepad++ and CCleaner. Kaspersky has not yet formally attributed but says evidence points to a Chinese-speaking actor.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-8302, a China-nexus APT operating since at least late 2024, that deploys multiple custom malware families (NetDraft .NET backdoor — a variant of FinalDraft/SquidDoor; an updated CloudSorcerer v3; VSHELL with the new Rust-based SNOWRUST stager; SNAPPYBEE/DeedRAT, ZingDoor, Draculoader). Initial access leverages both zero-day and n-day exploits; post-compromise tooling overlaps with Earth Estries, Earth Naga, Jewelbug/REF7707 and UNC5174.
incidents.impact: UAT-8302 is assessed as tasked with long-term access to government and related entities globally for intelligence collection. Talos' analysis underscores a tight tool-sharing relationship across the Chinese APT ecosystem, with one actor's custom toolkit reappearing across multiple clusters.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly compromised a Wasabi Protocol admin account and set the delay on admin actions to zero, allowing them to execute malicious cross-chain transactions instantly.
incidents.impact: $5 million in crypto assets stolen across multiple blockchains integrated with the Wasabi Protocol trading platform.

incidents.attacker: China — criminal espionage group (GoldenEyeDog / APT-Q-27 suspected)
incidents.vector: Attackers social-engineered two DigiCert tech-support staff into running a malicious .SCR screensaver file, then accessed in-flight EV code-signing certificate orders and stole the 'initialization codes' needed to claim the resulting certificates. One staff system retained attacker access for almost two weeks because the CrowdStrike EDR agent had been misconfigured and disconnected from its management console.
incidents.impact: 27 EV code-signing certificates were stolen and abused to sign Zhong Stealer payloads — malware historically linked to the Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog (APT-Q-27). DigiCert has revoked all 60 in-flight EV orders. The incident underlines the value of CA tech-support accounts as supply-chain targets.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Trellix's source-code repositories; the company has not disclosed the entry vector.
incidents.impact: Trellix says no changes were made to any of its products and has notified law enforcement. The breach is notable because Trellix is one of Europol's closest cybersecurity partners; source-code exposure could enable future targeted attacks against Trellix customers.

incidents.vector: The World Leaks hacking group breached Hungary's largest private news conglomerate Mediaworks and published internal files.
incidents.impact: The leak exposed meeting notes in which content directors said they would contact Moscow for help publishing anti-Ukraine content, a politically charged disclosure coming after Hungary's pro-Kremlin party lost the most recent elections. Mediaworks has sued a publication that covered the leak.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a recently disclosed cPanel vulnerability on shared hosting providers to wipe public websites and post a $8,000 Bitcoin ransom demand on their home pages ('fakestortion').
incidents.impact: Shadowserver reports more than 44,000 cPanel systems show signs of compromise — including the Government of Guam's web properties — though the attacker's wallet has not received any payments. The same bug is also being used to deploy cryptominers and DDoS malware.

incidents.victim: Republican Party of Alberta voter database (2.9M Albertans)
incidents.vector: The Republican Party of Alberta, a separatist political party, made a public searchable database containing personal data on 2.9 million Albertan voters available online.
incidents.impact: The database was taken down only after the provincial election agency sued. The mass exposure of voter PII by a political party — not by an outside intruder — illustrates the broader trend of voter data ending up in the hands of activist organizations with weak controls.
